manifest_note: The application has one external-authoring flow and makes no internal LLM or web-research calls. Scene Breakdown is one visible Studio stage with two external authoring steps: Step 1 locks semantic Scene/Beat state without publishing Project Scene/Visual pointers; Step 2 authors visuals against those exact locked IDs and atomically publishes the draft Scene Plan/Visual Plan pair. Scene Breakdown approval atomically publishes approved Scene Plan, Visual Plan, hidden Prompt Bundle, and BeatTimingMap. Scene Assets V2 stores working state and durable operations in database rows; its live standalone coordinator runner consumes the shared durable-media coordinator and provider-executor mechanics through Scene Asset domain adapters while Scene Asset BeatState CAS, prompt/reference validation, candidate materialization, continuity, and publication remain domain-owned. Visual References V2 is the canonical live Visual Reference runtime: durable AnchorState, immutable PromptRevision and Candidate lineage, DB-backed WorkingOperation/OperationAnchor/OperationTask execution, shared durable-media coordinator/provider execution, explicit immutable Reference Set and Approval Set publication, and targeted frontend refresh. Visual References is not owned by Redis/RQ. Voice is owned by the same Durable Media Workflow Host through VoiceGenerationOperation, VoiceSegmentTask, and VoiceAlignmentTask durable authority, ElevenLabs Professional Voice Clone presets, final-paced-WAV audio truth, Forced Alignment timing truth, fenced materialization/finalization, draft-candidate isolation, and approved Narration Audio + NarrationWordTimingMap publication. Voice is not owned by Redis/RQ; RQ production ownership is Render only. BeatTimingMap is Scene-owned and Assembly consumes it as the sole Beat visual timing authority. Provider I/O occurs outside database write transactions; provider submission ambiguity is never blindly retried; exact MediaTask transport ownership is fenced to durable operation tasks; generic startup recovery skips Visual Reference V2 transport so V2-specific recovery remains authoritative. No compatibility reader, dual-write, backfill, old-flow fallback, or schema adapter is active.
